world_constraints: The divine gift of weapons is tied to a particular grievance and bargain, explaining access but not arbitrary delivery.
The cache is exactly six cumbersome single-shot weapons with a finite supply of prepared charges.
Deliberate preparation, smoke, noise, imperfect aim and wet-weather failures limit use.
The weapons have visible material limits and cannot guarantee a hit or victory.
The Greeks interpret unfamiliar craft through their ancient experience.
Agamemnon claims the cache but depends on skilled men and coalition consent.
Hector and Achilles survive; larger political and divine conflicts remain open.
suggested_techniques: Use elevated English shaped by Homeric epic and an ancient social imagination throughout.
Retell from scratch: purely third person, no dialogue, no invocation.
Pin Iliad analysis work_136 as primary. Supplement only when it serves an actual gap.
Use material acts, reciprocal obligation, shame and rank; no stock modern cinematic gestures.
Roughly one extended comparison per scene when earned, no mandatory quota.
